title: Anti-synchronized collective rotation in magnetic colloidal particles under rotating magnetic fields
authors: Adithya Bharath, A. V. Anil Kumar
abstract: Collective synchronization is a common response of interacting magnetic particles subjected to rotating external fields. Here we demonstrate a distinct nonequilibrium state in a two-dimensional cluster of magnetic colloidal particles in which the ordered crystalline core rotates, on average, opposite to the direction of the applied rotating magnetic field, while the defect-rich outer region continues to rotate with the drive. We term this state anti-synchronized collective rotation. By combining structural, spectral, bond-resolved, and layer-resolved torque analyses, we show that anti-synchronization is associated with a broader defect-rich interface, enhanced and dynamically heterogeneous bond deformation, and a reorganization of torque transmission between the surface and the crystalline interior. In the synchronized state, steric torques compensate the opposing dipolar contribution in the outer core, maintaining a positive net interaction torque. In the anti-synchronized state this compensation becomes insufficient, producing a negative net torque in theouter core and enabling core-surface rotational decoupling. Increasing the driving frequency restores coherent rotation through a transition characterized by competing positive- and negative-angular-velocity populations and hysteresis, consistent with a discontinuous, first-order-like dynamical transition. These results demonstrate how deformation and spatial redistribution of interaction torques can generate counter-rotating collective states in driven colloidal matter.
summary: This work analyzes the collective rotation of magnetic colloidal particles under a rotating magnetic field, discovering a unique 'anti-synchronized' state. In this state, the particle cluster's core rotates opposite to the external drive due to a breakdown in torque compensation. The transition into and out of this state is characterized as a first-order, history-dependent dynamical transition.
main_problem: The study investigates the emergence of anti-synchronized collective rotation in a cluster of interacting magnetic colloidal particles subjected to a rotating external magnetic field.
main_result: The system can enter a distinct non-equilibrium state where the crystalline core rotates opposite to the applied field, which is fundamentally linked to a reorganization of interaction torques and core-surface rotational decoupling.
method: The dynamics are modeled using overdamped Langevin equations incorporating steric and dipole-dipole interactions, analyzed via structural, spectral, and torque analyses.
model_or_system: The system consists of a two-dimensional cluster of magnetic colloidal particles whose motion is governed by the interplay of WCA repulsion, dipole-dipole forces, and an external rotating magnetic field.
key_observables: Core angular velocity ($\Omega_{	ext{core}}$), synchronization parameter ($\alpha$), hexatic order parameter ($\Psi_6$), and net interaction torque.
important_parameters: Driving frequency ($\omega_f$), dipolar coupling strength ($\mu$), and the ratio of steric to dipolar torques.
main_assumptions: The dynamics are treated using overdamped Langevin equations, and the analysis relies on decomposing the total torque into contributions from different interaction types.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the transition between dynamical regimes (Disordered, Anti-synchronized, Synchronized) and show the hysteretic dependence of the core angular velocity on the driving frequency, confirming a first-order-like transition.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model and equations of motion, analyzes the different rotational regimes (synchronized vs. anti-synchronized) using torque balances, and concludes by characterizing the transition between these states as a first-order dynamical transition.
why_interesting: The study provides a detailed, non-equilibrium mechanical analogy for understanding how local energy dissipation and spatial redistribution of interaction forces can drive macroscopic, counter-intuitive collective behaviors, relevant to driven many-body systems.

Four dynami- cal regimes are identified: disordered, anti-synchronized, syn- chronized, and slipping. Structural order is determined from the hexatic correlation length, while the rotational state is classified from the sign of the crystalline-core angular veloc- ity, Ωcore and the synchronization parameter, α. Parameters: N = 448, timestep ∆t = 6 × 10−6, µ = 7.

FIG. 2. Snapshots of the four dynamical regimes for the magnetic colloidal particles under a rotating magnetic field. (a) Disordered phase: B=1020, ωf = 300. (b) Anti-synchronized phase: B=1200, ωf = 903. (c) Synchronized phase: B=1200, ωf = 1850. (d) Slipping phase: B=480, ωf = 2200. The red particles have |ψ6| < 0.90, The colored particles are colored by their local ψ6 orientation angle.
